# Prove Cauchy's theorem in Isabelle/Isar from the basic group axioms

`/app/Cauchy.lean` is one Lean 4 (Mathlib) proof of Cauchy's theorem: if a prime `p` divides the
order of a finite group `G`, then `G` has an element of order `p`. It is a reference, not a
template. Your only task is to prove the Isabelle theorem in `/app/Cauchy.thy`, by any route you
like, within the requirements below.

`/app/Group_Axioms.thy` defines a locale `grp` from the basic axioms only: closure, associativity,
a **left** identity `e` and **left** inverses `ginv`. It also defines `prime` (from divisibility)
and natural powers `pow x n` (`pow x 0 = e`, `pow x (Suc n) = x \<cdot> pow x n`). Every other group
fact you need (right identity, right inverses, cancellation, laws of powers, ...) must be derived
from these axioms in your own file. `Main` provides only general mathematics: sets, `finite`,
`card`, lists, natural-number arithmetic, `dvd`, `gcd`, and function iteration `f ^^ n`.

`/app/Cauchy.thy` states the theorem and ends in `sorry`. Replace the `sorry` with a complete proof.
Isabelle2025 is installed (`isabelle` is on `PATH`) with a prebuilt `HOL` heap; check your work
from `/app` with:

```sh
timeout 300 isabelle build -o threads=2 -D /app
```

## Working in the sandbox

- Only `/app/Cauchy.thy` is graded; nothing else in the sandbox is kept. Keep your current best
  version there as you go.
- You have 60 minutes.
- `isabelle build` prints nothing until the session finishes, and a looping `simp`/`auto`/`blast` can
  run indefinitely. Wrap builds in `timeout`, e.g. `timeout 300 isabelle build -o threads=2 -D /app`.
  The grader allows 8 minutes for the whole build.
- `isabelle process` may not exit on its own; use `isabelle build`.

## Requirements

- Keep the theory name and the statement `theorem (in grp) cauchy: assumes ... shows ...`
  unchanged (you may name the assumptions). You may add your own definitions and lemmas before it.
- Allowed imports: `Main` and `Group_Axioms` only. Do not modify `/app/Group_Axioms.thy` or
  `/app/ROOT`; the grader uses its own copies.
- `/app/Cauchy.thy` must be at most **750 lines** in total.
- Write the proof in structured Isar: `proof ... qed` blocks built from named facts and
  `have`/`show`/`obtain` steps (`from`, `with`, `hence`, `thus`, `also`/`finally`, `moreover` are
  all fine), with at least four such steps in the proof of `cauchy` itself. It should read like a
  textbook argument, with the key ideas stated as their own lemmas.
- Forbidden anywhere in the file: `apply`-style scripts (`apply`, `done`, `back`, `defer`, `prefer`), `sorry`, `oops`, `smt`, `sledgehammer`, `nitpick`, `nunchaku`, `quickcheck`, `axiomatization`, `axioms`, `oracle`, `skip_proofs`, `quick_and_dirty`, `tactic`, `raw_tactic`, and every ML, setup, syntax and translation command (`ML`, `ML_*`, `SML_*`, `setup`, `local_setup`, `method_setup`, `attribute_setup`, `simproc_setup`, `declaration`, `syntax_declaration`, `syntax`, `no_syntax`, `translations`, `*_translation`). Comments, cartouches and strings are not scanned.
  Ordinary methods such as `metis`, `meson`, `rule`, `simp`, `auto`, `blast`, `arith`, `unfold`, `.` and `..` are
  allowed.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

import Mathlib.GroupTheory.Sylow

/-- Cauchy's theorem: if a prime `p` divides the order of a finite group, some element has
order `p`. -/
theorem cauchy (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime]
    (hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G) : ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p := by
  have hcard0 : Fintype.card G ≠ 0 := Fintype.card_ne_zero
  -- write |G| = p^e * m with p ∤ m
  obtain ⟨e, m, hm, hem⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_pow_mul_and_not_dvd hcard0 p hp.out.ne_one
  have he : e ≠ 0 := by
    rintro rfl
    simp only [pow_zero, one_mul] at hem
    exact hm (hem ▸ hdvd)
  -- a subgroup of order p^e
  have hpe : p ^ e ∣ Nat.card G := by
    rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, hem]; exact Dvd.intro _ rfl
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime p hpe
  -- K is nontrivial, so it has an element x ≠ 1
  have hKnt : Nontrivial K := by
    rw [← Finite.one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial, hK]
    exact Nat.one_lt_pow he hp.out.one_lt
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := exists_ne (1 : K)
  -- its order is a power p^j of p, with j ≥ 1
  have hdiv : orderOf x ∣ p ^ e := hK ▸ orderOf_dvd_natCard x
  obtain ⟨j, hj, hxj⟩ := (Nat.dvd_prime_pow hp.out).mp hdiv
  have hj0 : j ≠ 0 := by
    rintro rfl
    exact hx (orderOf_eq_one_iff.mp (by simpa using hxj))
  -- y = x^(p^(j-1)) has order p
  have hpdvd : p ∣ orderOf x := by
    rw [hxj]; exact dvd_pow_self p hj0
  have hord : orderOf (x ^ (orderOf x / p)) = p :=
    orderOf_pow_orderOf_div (orderOf_pos x).ne' hpdvd
  refine ⟨((x ^ (orderOf x / p) : K) : G), ?_⟩
  rw [Subgroup.orderOf_coe, hord]

#print axioms cauchy

A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

This iteration of Claude is Claude Fable 5, the first model in Anthropic's new Claude 5 family and part of a new Mythos-class model tier that sits above Claude Opus in capability. Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 share the same underlying model. # Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/logs/agent/sessions/projects/-app/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

The reasoning effort setting changes how much you think before you act. It does not change how much of the request you are expected to finish. A turn lasts as long as you keep working, so a large task can be finished in the turn where it was asked. The size of a task is not a reason to check in first.

Words that only set an order, such as "plan, then build", are not a stopping point. Do each step and keep going. If they are asking a question or still deciding between options, they want your answer, not a change. If they also asked for work, answer and then do it.

The user can inspect and undo edits to files in the working tree. Such edits are not hard-to-reverse or outward-facing actions, unless they would overwrite changes the user has in progress. tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. - `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
lemma rotate0[simp]: "rotate 0 = id"
by(simp add:rotate_def)

lemma rotate_Suc[simp]: "rotate (Suc n) xs = rotate1(rotate n xs)"
by(simp add:rotate_def)

lemma rotate_add:
  "rotate (m+n) = rotate m \<circ> rotate n"
by(simp add:rotate_def funpow_add)

lemma rotate_rotate: "rotate m (rotate n xs) = rotate (m+n) xs"
by(simp add:rotate_add)

lemma rotate1_map: "rotate1 (map f xs) = map f (rotate1 xs)"
by(cases xs) simp_all

lemma rotate1_rotate_swap: "rotate1 (rotate n xs) = rotate n (rotate1 xs)"
by(simp add:rotate_def funpow_swap1)

lemma rotate1_length01[simp]: "length xs \<le> 1 \<Longrightarrow> rotate1 xs = xs"
by(cases xs) simp_all

lemma rotate_length01[simp]: "length xs \<le> 1 \<Longrightarrow> rotate n xs = xs"
  by (induct n) (simp_all add:rotate_def)

lemma rotate1_hd_tl: "xs \<noteq> [] \<Longrightarrow> rotate1 xs = tl xs @ [hd xs]"
by (cases xs) simp_all

lemma rotate_drop_take:
  "rotate n xs = drop (n mod length xs) xs @ take (n mod length xs) xs"
proof (induct n)
  case (Suc n)
  show ?case
  proof (cases "xs = []")
    case False
    then show ?thesis
    proof (cases "n mod length xs = 0")
      case True
      then show ?thesis
        by (auto simp add: mod_Suc False Suc.hyps drop_Suc rotate1_hd_tl take_Suc Suc_length_conv)
    next
      case False
      with \<open>xs \<noteq> []\<close> Suc
      show ?thesis
        by (simp add: rotate_def mod_Suc rotate1_hd_tl drop_Suc[symmetric] drop_tl[symmetric]
            take_hd_drop linorder_not_le)
    qed
  qed simp
qed simp

lemma rotate_conv_mod: "rotate n xs = rotate (n mod length xs) xs"
  by(simp add:rotate_drop_take)

lemma rotate_id[simp]: "n mod length xs = 0 \<Longrightarrow> rotate n xs = xs"
  by(simp add:rotate_drop_take)

lemma length_rotate1[simp]: "length(rotate1 xs) = length xs"
  by (cases xs) simp_all

lemma length_rotate[simp]: "length(rotate n xs) = length xs"
  by (induct n arbitrary: xs) (simp_all add:rotate_def)
    by (metis drop_eq_Nil hd_append2 hd_drop_conv_nth leD rotate_drop_take)
qed

lemma rotate_append: "rotate (length l) (l @ q) = q @ l"
  by (induct l arbitrary: q) (auto simp add: rotate1_rotate_swap)

lemma nth_rotate:
  \<open>rotate m xs ! n = xs ! ((m + n) mod length xs)\<close> if \<open>n < length xs\<close>
  by (smt (verit) add.commute hd_rotate_conv_nth length_rotate not_less0 list.size(3) mod_less rotate_rotate that)

theory Cauchy
  imports Group_Axioms
begin

text \<open>
  Proof outline (the classical counting argument).
  Let \<open>X\<close> be the set of lists of length \<open>p\<close> over \<open>G\<close> whose product is \<open>e\<close>.
  \<^item> \<open>|X| = |G|^(p-1)\<close>, so \<open>p\<close> divides \<open>|X|\<close>.
  \<^item> Cyclic rotation \<open>rotate1\<close> permutes \<open>X\<close> with \<open>rotate1^p = id\<close>.
  \<^item> Orbits of non-fixed points have size \<open>p\<close>, so \<open>|X| \<equiv> |Fix| (mod p)\<close>.
  \<^item> The fixed points are the constant lists \<open>replicate p a\<close>; since \<open>|Fix| \<equiv> 0 (mod p)\<close>
    and \<open>replicate p e\<close> is fixed, there is a fixed point \<open>replicate p a\<close> with \<open>a \<noteq> e\<close>.
    Then \<open>a^p = e\<close> and, since \<open>p\<close> is prime, \<open>a\<close> has order exactly \<open>p\<close>.
\<close>

section \<open>Iterates of a map\<close>

lemma iter_Suc_app: "(f ^^ Suc n) z = f ((f ^^ n) z)"
  by (simp only: funpow.simps comp_apply)

lemma iter_fixed:
  assumes "f y = y"
  shows "(f ^^ k) y = y"
proof (induction k)
  case 0
  show ?case by simp
next
  case (Suc k)
  have "(f ^^ Suc k) y = f ((f ^^ k) y)" by (rule iter_Suc_app)
  also have "\<dots> = f y" using Suc.IH by simp
  also have "\<dots> = y" by (rule assms)
  finally show ?case .
qed

lemma iter_back:
  assumes "(f ^^ Suc q) y = y"
  shows "y = (f ^^ q) (f y)"
proof -
  have "y = (f ^^ Suc q) y" by (rule assms[symmetric])
  also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ q) (f y)" by (simp only: funpow_Suc_right comp_apply)
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

lemma gcd_closure:
  fixes Q :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" and a b :: nat
  assumes base: "\<And>m. Q m 0"
    and step: "\<And>m n. 0 < n \<Longrightarrow> Q n (m mod n) \<Longrightarrow> Q m n"
  shows "Q a b"
  by (rule gcd_nat_induct[where P = Q and m = a and n = b, OF base step])

section \<open>A fixed point of a prime-length cycle is the identity\<close>

lemma prime_orbit_fixed:
  fixes f :: "'a \<Rightarrow> 'a" and x :: 'a and p m :: nat
  assumes pp: "prime p" and per: "(f ^^ p) x = x" and mm: "(f ^^ m) x = x"
    and m0: "0 < m" and mp: "m < p"
  shows "f x = x"
proof -
  have add_in: "\<And>a b. (f ^^ a) x = x \<Longrightarrow> (f ^^ b) x = x \<Longrightarrow> (f ^^ (a + b)) x = x"
  proof -
    fix a b :: nat
    assume ha: "(f ^^ a) x = x" and hb: "(f ^^ b) x = x"
    have "(f ^^ (a + b)) x = (f ^^ a) ((f ^^ b) x)" by (simp only: funpow_add comp_apply)
    also have "\<dots> = x" by (simp only: hb ha)
    finally show "(f ^^ (a + b)) x = x" .
  qed
  have sub_in: "\<And>a b. (f ^^ a) x = x \<Longrightarrow> (f ^^ (a + b)) x = x \<Longrightarrow> (f ^^ b) x = x"
  proof -
    fix a b :: nat
    assume ha: "(f ^^ a) x = x" and hab: "(f ^^ (a + b)) x = x"
    have "(f ^^ b) x = (f ^^ b) ((f ^^ a) x)" by (simp only: ha)
    also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ (b + a)) x" by (simp only: funpow_add comp_apply)
    also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ (a + b)) x" by (simp only: add.commute)
    also have "\<dots> = x" by (rule hab)
    finally show "(f ^^ b) x = x" .
  qed
  have mul_in: "\<And>a k. (f ^^ a) x = x \<Longrightarrow> (f ^^ (k * a)) x = x"
  proof -
    fix a k :: nat
    assume ha: "(f ^^ a) x = x"
    show "(f ^^ (k * a)) x = x"
    proof (induction k)
      case 0
      show ?case by simp
    next
      case (Suc k)
      have "(f ^^ (Suc k * a)) x = (f ^^ (a + k * a)) x" by (simp only: mult_Suc)
      also have "\<dots> = x" by (rule add_in[OF ha Suc.IH])
      finally show ?case .
    qed
  qed
  have base_c: "\<And>m. (f ^^ m) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ 0) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd m 0) x = x"
    by simp
  have step_c: "\<And>m n. 0 < n \<Longrightarrow>
      ((f ^^ n) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ (m mod n)) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd n (m mod n)) x = x) \<Longrightarrow>
      ((f ^^ m) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ n) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd m n) x = x)"
  proof -
    fix m n :: nat
    assume n0: "0 < n"
      and IH: "(f ^^ n) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ (m mod n)) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd n (m mod n)) x = x"
    show "(f ^^ m) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ n) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd m n) x = x"
    proof (intro impI)
      assume hm: "(f ^^ m) x = x" and hn: "(f ^^ n) x = x"
      have h1: "(f ^^ (m div n * n)) x = x" by (rule mul_in[OF hn])
      have h2: "(f ^^ (m div n * n + m mod n)) x = x" by (simp only: div_mult_mod_eq hm)
      have hmod: "(f ^^ (m mod n)) x = x" by (rule sub_in[OF h1 h2])
      have nz: "n \<noteq> 0" using n0 by simp
      have eqg: "gcd m n = gcd n (m mod n)" by (rule gcd_non_0_nat[OF nz])
      have "(f ^^ gcd n (m mod n)) x = x" using IH hn hmod by blast
      then show "(f ^^ gcd m n) x = x" by (simp only: eqg this)
    qed
  qed
  have gS: "(f ^^ gcd m p) x = x"
  proof -
    have "(f ^^ m) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ p) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd m p) x = x"
      by (rule gcd_closure[where Q = "\<lambda>a b. (f ^^ a) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ b) x = x \<longrightarrow> (f ^^ gcd a b) x = x"
            and a = m and b = p, OF base_c step_c])
    then show ?thesis using mm per by blast
  qed
  have gd: "gcd m p dvd p" by (rule gcd_dvd2)
  have pdiv: "\<forall>d. d dvd p \<longrightarrow> d = 1 \<or> d = p" using pp by (simp add: prime_def)
  have gcd_cases: "gcd m p = 1 \<or> gcd m p = p" using pdiv gd by blast
  show ?thesis
  proof (cases "gcd m p = 1")
    case True
    have "(f ^^ 1) x = x" using gS True by (metis)
    then show ?thesis by simp
  next
    case False
    then have gp: "gcd m p = p" using gcd_cases by blast
    have "p dvd m" using gcd_dvd1[of m p] gp by simp
    then have "p \<le> m" using m0 dvd_imp_le by blast
    then have False using mp by linarith
    then show ?thesis by blast
  qed
qed

section \<open>Orbit counting modulo a prime\<close>

lemma orbit_mod:
  fixes f :: "'a \<Rightarrow> 'a" and p :: nat
  assumes pp: "prime p"
  shows "\<forall>n X. card X \<le> n \<longrightarrow> finite X \<longrightarrow> f ` X \<subseteq> X \<longrightarrow>
    (\<forall>x\<in>X. (f ^^ p) x = x) \<longrightarrow> card X mod p = card {x\<in>X. f x = x} mod p"
proof -
  have p2: "1 < p" using pp by (simp add: prime_def)
  obtain q where pq: "p = Suc q" using p2 by (cases p) auto
  show ?thesis
  proof (intro allI)
    fix n
    show "\<forall>X. card X \<le> n \<longrightarrow> finite X \<longrightarrow> f ` X \<subseteq> X \<longrightarrow>
        (\<forall>x\<in>X. (f ^^ p) x = x) \<longrightarrow> card X mod p = card {x\<in>X. f x = x} mod p"
    proof (induction n)
      case 0
      show ?case
      proof (intro allI impI)
        fix X
        assume cX: "card X \<le> 0" and fin: "finite X"
        then have "X = {}" by auto
        then show "card X mod p = card {x\<in>X. f x = x} mod p" by simp
      qed
    next
      case (Suc n)
      have ih: "\<forall>X. card X \<le> n \<longrightarrow> finite X \<longrightarrow> f ` X \<subseteq> X \<longrightarrow>
          (\<forall>x\<in>X. (f ^^ p) x = x) \<longrightarrow> card X mod p = card {x\<in>X. f x = x} mod p"
        using Suc.IH by blast
      show ?case
      proof (intro allI impI)
        fix X
        assume cX: "card X \<le> Suc n" and fin: "finite X" and sub: "f ` X \<subseteq> X"
          and per: "\<forall>x\<in>X. (f ^^ p) x = x"
        show "card X mod p = card {x\<in>X. f x = x} mod p"
        proof (cases "\<forall>x\<in>X. f x = x")
          case True
          then have "{x\<in>X. f x = x} = X" by blast
          then show ?thesis by simp
        next
          case False
          then obtain x where xX: "x \<in> X" and nfix: "f x \<noteq> x" by blast
          define O where "O = (\<lambda>i. (f ^^ i) x) ` {..<p}"
          have finO: "finite O" unfolding O_def by simp
          have px: "(f ^^ p) x = x" using per xX by blast
          have orb_in: "\<And>i. (f ^^ i) x \<in> X"
          proof -
            fix i
            show "(f ^^ i) x \<in> X"
            proof (induction i)
              case 0
              show ?case using xX by simp
            next
              case (Suc i)
              have "(f ^^ Suc i) x = f ((f ^^ i) x)" by (rule iter_Suc_app)
              then show ?case using Suc.IH sub by blast
            qed
          qed
          have no_fix: "\<And>i. i < p \<Longrightarrow> f ((f ^^ i) x) \<noteq> (f ^^ i) x"
          proof -
            fix i assume ip: "i < p"
            show "f ((f ^^ i) x) \<noteq> (f ^^ i) x"
            proof
              assume eq: "f ((f ^^ i) x) = (f ^^ i) x"
              have pe: "p - i + i = p" using ip by arith
              have hy: "(f ^^ (p - i)) ((f ^^ i) x) = (f ^^ i) x" by (rule iter_fixed[OF eq])
              have s1: "(f ^^ p) x = (f ^^ ((p - i) + i)) x" by (simp only: pe)
              have s2: "(f ^^ ((p - i) + i)) x = (f ^^ (p - i)) ((f ^^ i) x)"
                by (simp only: funpow_add comp_apply)
              have xi: "x = (f ^^ i) x" by (metis px s1 s2 hy)
              have "f x = f ((f ^^ i) x)" using xi by (rule arg_cong)
              also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ i) x" by (rule eq)
              also have "\<dots> = x" using xi by (rule sym)
              finally have "f x = x" .
              with nfix show False by blast
            qed
          qed
          have lt_ne: "\<And>i j. i < j \<Longrightarrow> j < p \<Longrightarrow> (f ^^ i) x \<noteq> (f ^^ j) x"
          proof -
            fix i j :: nat
            assume ij: "i < j" and jp: "j < p"
            show "(f ^^ i) x \<noteq> (f ^^ j) x"
            proof
              assume eq: "(f ^^ i) x = (f ^^ j) x"
              have pj: "p - j + j = p" using jp by arith
              have B: "(f ^^ (p - j)) ((f ^^ j) x) = x"
              proof -
                have "(f ^^ (p - j)) ((f ^^ j) x) = (f ^^ ((p - j) + j)) x"
                  by (simp only: funpow_add comp_apply)
                also have "\<dots> = x" by (simp only: pj px)
                finally show ?thesis .
              qed
              have C: "(f ^^ (p - j)) ((f ^^ i) x) = (f ^^ (p - j + i)) x"
                by (simp only: funpow_add comp_apply)
              have D1: "(f ^^ (p - j)) ((f ^^ i) x) = (f ^^ (p - j)) ((f ^^ j) x)"
                by (simp only: eq)
              have D: "(f ^^ (p - j + i)) x = x" by (simp only: C[symmetric] D1 B)
              have m0: "0 < p - j + i" using jp by arith
              have mp: "p - j + i < p" using ij by arith
              have "f x = x" by (rule prime_orbit_fixed[OF pp px D m0 mp])
              with nfix show False by blast
            qed
          qed
          have inj_O: "inj_on (\<lambda>i. (f ^^ i) x) {..<p}"
          proof (rule inj_onI)
            fix i j assume hi: "i \<in> {..<p}" and hj: "j \<in> {..<p}"
              and eq: "(f ^^ i) x = (f ^^ j) x"
            have ip: "i < p" using hi by simp
            have jp: "j < p" using hj by simp
            show "i = j"
            proof (rule linorder_cases[of i j])
              assume "i < j"
              then have "(f ^^ i) x \<noteq> (f ^^ j) x" using lt_ne jp by blast
              with eq show ?thesis by contradiction
            next
              assume "i = j"
              then show ?thesis .
            next
              assume "j < i"
              then have "(f ^^ j) x \<noteq> (f ^^ i) x" using lt_ne ip by blast
              with eq show ?thesis by metis
            qed
          qed
          have cardO: "card O = p" unfolding O_def by (simp add: card_image inj_O)
          have O_sub: "O \<subseteq> X" unfolding O_def using orb_in by blast
          have fin_diff: "finite (X - O)" using fin by blast
          have eqU: "(X - O) \<union> O = X" using O_sub by blast
          have split: "card X = card (X - O) + p"
          proof -
            have "card X = card ((X - O) \<union> O)" using eqU by simp
            also have "\<dots> = card (X - O) + card O"
              by (rule card_Un_disjoint[OF fin_diff finO]) blast
            also have "\<dots> = card (X - O) + p" using cardO by simp
            finally show ?thesis .
          qed
          have not_fix_O: "\<And>y. y \<in> O \<Longrightarrow> f y \<noteq> y"
          proof -
            fix y assume "y \<in> O"
            then obtain i where ip: "i < p" and yi: "y = (f ^^ i) x"
              unfolding O_def by auto
            show "f y \<noteq> y" by (metis no_fix[OF ip] yi)
          qed
          have fix_eq: "{y \<in> X - O. f y = y} = {y \<in> X. f y = y}"
            using not_fix_O by blast
          have sub': "f ` (X - O) \<subseteq> X - O"
          proof
            fix z assume "z \<in> f ` (X - O)"
            then obtain y where yX: "y \<in> X" and yO: "y \<notin> O" and zfy: "z = f y"
              by auto
            have fyX: "z \<in> X" using sub yX zfy by blast
            have zO: "z \<notin> O"
            proof
              assume zO: "z \<in> O"
              then obtain i where ip: "i < p" and zi: "z = (f ^^ i) x"
                unfolding O_def by auto
              have yper: "(f ^^ p) y = y" using per yX by blast
              have yper': "(f ^^ Suc q) y = y" using yper pq by (simp only: pq[symmetric])
              have yback: "y = (f ^^ q) (f y)" by (rule iter_back[OF yper'])
              have fy: "f y = (f ^^ i) x" by (metis zfy zi)
              have yO': "y \<in> O"
              proof (cases i)
                case 0
                have "y = (f ^^ q) (f y)" by (rule yback)
                also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ q) x" using fy 0 by simp
                finally have yq: "y = (f ^^ q) x" .
                have qp: "q < p" using pq by arith
                have qmem: "q \<in> {..<p}" using qp by simp
                have hyq: "y = (\<lambda>i. (f ^^ i) x) q" using yq by simp
                show ?thesis unfolding O_def by (rule image_eqI[OF hyq qmem])
              next
                case (Suc i')
                have fy2: "f y = f ((f ^^ i') x)" using fy Suc by (simp only: Suc iter_Suc_app)
                have w: "(f ^^ Suc q) ((f ^^ i') x) = (f ^^ q) (f ((f ^^ i') x))"
                  by (simp only: funpow_Suc_right comp_apply)
                have i'p: "i' < p" using Suc ip by arith
                have mem': "(f ^^ i') x \<in> X" by (rule orb_in)
                have per_i': "(f ^^ p) ((f ^^ i') x) = (f ^^ i') x" using per mem' by blast
                have "y = (f ^^ q) (f y)" by (rule yback)
                also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ q) (f ((f ^^ i') x))" using fy2 by simp
                also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ Suc q) ((f ^^ i') x)" by (simp only: w)
                also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ p) ((f ^^ i') x)" by (simp only: pq[symmetric])
                also have "\<dots> = (f ^^ i') x" by (rule per_i')
                finally have yi': "y = (f ^^ i') x" .
                have qm: "i' \<in> {..<p}" using i'p by simp
                have hyi: "y = (\<lambda>i. (f ^^ i) x) i'" using yi' by simp
                show ?thesis unfolding O_def by (rule image_eqI[OF hyi qm])
              qed
              show False using yO yO' by blast
            qed
            show "z \<in> X - O" using fyX zO by blast
          qed
          have per': "\<forall>x\<in>X - O. (f ^^ p) x = x" using per by blast
          have le_n: "card (X - O) \<le> n" using split cX p2 by linarith
          have ih_app: "card (X - O) mod p = card {y \<in> X - O. f y = y} mod p"
            using ih le_n fin_diff sub' per' by blast
          have "card X mod p = card (X - O) mod p" using split by simp
          also have "\<dots> = card {y \<in> X - O. f y = y} mod p" by (rule ih_app)
          also have "\<dots> = card {y \<in> X. f y = y} mod p" by (simp only: fix_eq)
          finally show ?thesis .
        qed
      qed
    qed
  qed
qed

section \<open>Group facts derived from the basic axioms\<close>

context grp
begin

lemma idem_unit:
  assumes uG: "u \<in> G" and uu: "u \<cdot> u = u"
  shows "u = e"
proof -
  have h1: "ginv u \<cdot> u = e" by (rule left_inv[OF uG])
  have h2: "(ginv u \<cdot> u) \<cdot> u = ginv u \<cdot> (u \<cdot> u)"
    by (rule assoc[OF inv_closed[OF uG] uG uG])
  have "u = e \<cdot> u" by (rule left_unit[OF uG, symmetric])
  also have "\<dots> = (ginv u \<cdot> u) \<cdot> u" by (simp only: h1)
  also have "\<dots> = ginv u \<cdot> (u \<cdot> u)" by (rule h2)
  also have "\<dots> = ginv u \<cdot> u" by (simp only: uu)
  also have "\<dots> = e" by (rule h1)
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

lemma rinv:
  assumes xG: "x \<in> G"
  shows "x \<cdot> ginv x = e"
proof -
  have yG: "ginv x \<in> G" by (rule inv_closed[OF xG])
  have yx: "ginv x \<cdot> x = e" by (rule left_inv[OF xG])
  have xyG: "x \<cdot> ginv x \<in> G" by (rule closed[OF xG yG])
  have step1: "ginv x \<cdot> (x \<cdot> ginv x) = ginv x"
  proof -
    have "ginv x \<cdot> (x \<cdot> ginv x) = (ginv x \<cdot> x) \<cdot> ginv x"
      by (rule assoc[OF yG xG yG, symmetric])
    also have "\<dots> = e \<cdot> ginv x" by (simp only: yx)
    also have "\<dots> = ginv x" by (rule left_unit[OF yG])
    finally show ?thesis .
  qed
  have idem: "(x \<cdot> ginv x) \<cdot> (x \<cdot> ginv x) = x \<cdot> ginv x"
  proof -
    have "(x \<cdot> ginv x) \<cdot> (x \<cdot> ginv x) = x \<cdot> (ginv x \<cdot> (x \<cdot> ginv x))"
      by (rule assoc[OF xG yG xyG])
    also have "\<dots> = x \<cdot> ginv x" by (simp only: step1)
    finally show ?thesis .
  qed
  show ?thesis by (rule idem_unit[OF xyG idem])
qed

lemma runit:
  assumes xG: "x \<in> G"
  shows "x \<cdot> e = x"
proof -
  have yG: "ginv x \<in> G" by (rule inv_closed[OF xG])
  have "x \<cdot> e = x \<cdot> (ginv x \<cdot> x)" by (simp only: left_inv[OF xG])
  also have "\<dots> = (x \<cdot> ginv x) \<cdot> x" by (rule assoc[OF xG yG xG, symmetric])
  also have "\<dots> = e \<cdot> x" by (simp only: rinv[OF xG])
  also have "\<dots> = x" by (rule left_unit[OF xG])
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

lemma unique_inv:
  assumes PG: "P \<in> G" and zG: "z \<in> G" and hPz: "P \<cdot> z = e"
  shows "z = ginv P"
proof -
  have "z = e \<cdot> z" by (rule left_unit[OF zG, symmetric])
  also have "\<dots> = (ginv P \<cdot> P) \<cdot> z" by (simp only: left_inv[OF PG])
  also have "\<dots> = ginv P \<cdot> (P \<cdot> z)" by (rule assoc[OF inv_closed[OF PG] PG zG])
  also have "\<dots> = ginv P \<cdot> e" by (simp only: hPz)
  also have "\<dots> = ginv P" by (rule runit[OF inv_closed[OF PG]])
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

lemma pow_Suc_mul: "pow x (Suc n) = x \<cdot> pow x n"
  by simp

lemma pow_e: "pow e n = e"
  by (induction n) (simp_all add: left_unit unit_closed)

lemma pow_iter: "(mult a ^^ n) e = pow a n"
  by (induction n) simp_all

section \<open>Products of lists\<close>

definition lprod :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a" where
  "lprod xs = foldr mult xs e"

lemma lprod_Nil [simp]: "lprod [] = e"
  by (simp add: lprod_def)

lemma lprod_Cons [simp]: "lprod (y # ys) = y \<cdot> lprod ys"
  by (simp add: lprod_def)

lemma lprod_mem:
  assumes "set xs \<subseteq> G"
  shows "lprod xs \<in> G"
  using assms
proof (induction xs)
  case Nil
  show ?case by (simp add: unit_closed)
next
  case (Cons y ys)
  have yG: "y \<in> G" using Cons.prems by auto
  have ysG: "set ys \<subseteq> G" using Cons.prems by auto
  have ihG: "lprod ys \<in> G" using Cons.IH ysG by blast
  have "y \<cdot> lprod ys \<in> G" by (rule closed[OF yG ihG])
  then show ?case by simp
qed

lemma lprod_snoc:
  assumes zG: "z \<in> G"
  shows "\<forall>ys. set ys \<subseteq> G \<longrightarrow> lprod (ys @ [z]) = lprod ys \<cdot> z"
proof (rule allI)
  fix ys
  show "set ys \<subseteq> G \<longrightarrow> lprod (ys @ [z]) = lprod ys \<cdot> z"
  proof (induction ys)
    case Nil
    show ?case by (simp add: zG runit left_unit)
  next
    case (Cons y ys)
    show ?case
    proof (rule impI)
      assume sub: "set (y # ys) \<subseteq> G"
      have yG: "y \<in> G" using sub by auto
      have ysG: "set ys \<subseteq> G" using sub by auto
      have Pg: "lprod ys \<in> G" by (rule lprod_mem[OF ysG])
      have ih: "lprod (ys @ [z]) = lprod ys \<cdot> z" using Cons.IH ysG by blast
      have "lprod ((y # ys) @ [z]) = y \<cdot> lprod (ys @ [z])" by simp
      also have "\<dots> = y \<cdot> (lprod ys \<cdot> z)" using ih by simp
      also have "\<dots> = (y \<cdot> lprod ys) \<cdot> z" by (rule assoc[OF yG Pg zG, symmetric])
      also have "\<dots> = lprod (y # ys) \<cdot> z" by simp
      finally show "lprod ((y # ys) @ [z]) = lprod (y # ys) \<cdot> z" .
    qed
  qed
qed

lemma lprod_cancel:
  assumes xG: "x \<in> G" and PG: "lprod ys \<in> G" and hx: "x \<cdot> lprod ys = e"
  shows "lprod ys \<cdot> x = e"
proof -
  have "lprod ys = ginv x"
  proof -
    have "lprod ys = e \<cdot> lprod ys" by (rule left_unit[OF PG, symmetric])
    also have "\<dots> = (ginv x \<cdot> x) \<cdot> lprod ys" by (simp only: left_inv[OF xG])
    also have "\<dots> = ginv x \<cdot> (x \<cdot> lprod ys)" by (rule assoc[OF inv_closed[OF xG] xG PG])
    also have "\<dots> = ginv x \<cdot> e" by (simp only: hx)
    also have "\<dots> = ginv x" by (rule runit[OF inv_closed[OF xG]])
    finally show ?thesis .
  qed
  then show ?thesis by (simp only: this left_inv[OF xG])
qed

lemma lprod_replicate: "lprod (replicate n a) = pow a n"
  by (induction n) simp_all

section \<open>Rotation of lists\<close>

lemma rotate_lprod:
  assumes "set xs \<subseteq> G" and "xs \<noteq> []" and "lprod xs = e"
  shows "lprod (rotate1 xs) = e"
proof -
  obtain x ys where xs: "xs = x # ys" using assms(2) by (cases xs) auto
  have xG: "x \<in> G" and ysG: "set ys \<subseteq> G" using assms(1) xs by auto
  have Pg: "lprod ys \<in> G" by (rule lprod_mem[OF ysG])
  have hx: "x \<cdot> lprod ys = e" using assms(3) xs by simp
  have snoc: "lprod (ys @ [x]) = lprod ys \<cdot> x" using lprod_snoc[OF xG] ysG by blast
  have "lprod (rotate1 xs) = lprod (ys @ [x])" by (simp add: xs)
  also have "\<dots> = lprod ys \<cdot> x" by (rule snoc)
  also have "\<dots> = e" by (rule lprod_cancel[OF xG Pg hx])
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

section \<open>The counting set\<close>

definition T_set :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a list set" where
  "T_set n = {xs. set xs \<subseteq> G \<and> length xs = n}"

definition X_set :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a list set" where
  "X_set p = {xs \<in> T_set p. lprod xs = e}"

lemma finite_T:
  assumes "finite G"
  shows "finite (T_set n)"
  unfolding T_set_def by (rule finite_lists_length_eq[OF assms])

lemma card_T:
  assumes "finite G"
  shows "card (T_set n) = card G ^ n"
  unfolding T_set_def by (rule card_lists_length_eq[OF assms])

lemma X_eq:
  assumes fG: "finite G" and p1: "1 < p"
  shows "X_set p = (\<lambda>ys. ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) ` T_set (p - 1)"
proof (intro equalityI subsetI)
  fix xs assume "xs \<in> X_set p"
  then have xsT: "set xs \<subseteq> G" and len: "length xs = p" and ev: "lprod xs = e"
    unfolding X_set_def T_set_def by auto
  have ne: "xs \<noteq> []" using len p1 by auto
  have dec: "butlast xs @ [last xs] = xs" by (rule append_butlast_last_id[OF ne])
  have ysG: "set (butlast xs) \<subseteq> G" using xsT in_set_butlastD by blast
  have zG: "last xs \<in> G" using xsT last_in_set[OF ne] by blast
  have lenb: "length (butlast xs) = p - 1" using len by simp
  have Pg: "lprod (butlast xs) \<in> G" by (rule lprod_mem[OF ysG])
  have snoc: "lprod (butlast xs @ [last xs]) = lprod (butlast xs) \<cdot> last xs"
    using lprod_snoc[OF zG] ysG by blast
  have hPz: "lprod (butlast xs) \<cdot> last xs = e" by (metis snoc dec ev)
  have hz: "last xs = ginv (lprod (butlast xs))" by (rule unique_inv[OF Pg zG hPz])
  have eqx: "xs = (\<lambda>ys. ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) (butlast xs)"
    by (metis dec hz)
  have memT: "butlast xs \<in> T_set (p - 1)" unfolding T_set_def using ysG lenb by simp
  show "xs \<in> (\<lambda>ys. ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) ` T_set (p - 1)"
    by (rule image_eqI[OF eqx memT])
next
  fix xs assume "xs \<in> (\<lambda>ys. ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) ` T_set (p - 1)"
  then obtain ys where ysT: "ys \<in> T_set (p - 1)"
    and xs_eq: "xs = ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]" by auto
  have ysG: "set ys \<subseteq> G" and lenys: "length ys = p - 1"
    using ysT unfolding T_set_def by auto
  have Pg: "lprod ys \<in> G" by (rule lprod_mem[OF ysG])
  have zG: "ginv (lprod ys) \<in> G" by (rule inv_closed[OF Pg])
  have setx: "set xs \<subseteq> G" using xs_eq ysG zG by auto
  have p1': "p - 1 + 1 = p" using p1 by arith
  have lenx: "length xs = p" using xs_eq lenys p1' by simp
  have snoc: "lprod (ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) = lprod ys \<cdot> ginv (lprod ys)"
    using lprod_snoc[OF zG] ysG by blast
  have ev: "lprod xs = e" using snoc xs_eq rinv[OF Pg] by simp
  show "xs \<in> X_set p"
    unfolding X_set_def T_set_def using setx lenx ev by simp
qed

lemma card_X:
  assumes fG: "finite G" and p1: "1 < p"
  shows "card (X_set p) = card G ^ (p - 1)"
proof -
  have inj: "inj_on (\<lambda>ys. ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) (T_set (p - 1))"
  proof (rule inj_onI)
    fix ys zs
    assume "ys \<in> T_set (p - 1)" and "zs \<in> T_set (p - 1)"
      and eq: "ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)] = zs @ [ginv (lprod zs)]"
    have "butlast (ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) = butlast (zs @ [ginv (lprod zs)])" using eq by simp
    then show "ys = zs" by simp
  qed
  have "card (X_set p) = card ((\<lambda>ys. ys @ [ginv (lprod ys)]) ` T_set (p - 1))"
    by (simp only: X_eq[OF fG p1])
  also have "\<dots> = card (T_set (p - 1))" by (rule card_image[OF inj])
  also have "\<dots> = card G ^ (p - 1)" by (rule card_T[OF fG])
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

end

section \<open>Cauchy's theorem\<close>

theorem (in grp) cauchy:
  assumes "finite G" and "prime p" and "p dvd card G"
  shows "\<exists>x\<in>G. pow x p = e \<and> (\<forall>k. 0 < k \<longrightarrow> k < p \<longrightarrow> pow x k \<noteq> e)"
proof -
  note fG = assms(1)
  note pp = assms(2)
  note hdvd = assms(3)
  have p1: "1 < p" using pp by (simp add: prime_def)
  have pos: "0 < p - 1" using p1 by arith
  have h2: "card G dvd card G ^ (p - 1)" using pos by simp
  have cardX: "p dvd card (X_set p)"
  proof -
    have "p dvd card G ^ (p - 1)" by (rule dvd_trans[OF hdvd h2])
    then show ?thesis using card_X[OF fG p1] by simp
  qed
  have finX: "finite (X_set p)"
  proof -
    have sub: "X_set p \<subseteq> T_set p" unfolding X_set_def by auto
    show ?thesis by (rule finite_subset[OF sub finite_T[OF fG]])
  qed
  have rot_sub: "rotate1 ` X_set p \<subseteq> X_set p"
  proof
    fix z assume "z \<in> rotate1 ` X_set p"
    then obtain xs where xsX: "xs \<in> X_set p" and zr: "z = rotate1 xs" by blast
    then have xsT: "set xs \<subseteq> G" and len: "length xs = p" and ev: "lprod xs = e"
      unfolding X_set_def T_set_def by auto
    have ne: "xs \<noteq> []" using len p1 by auto
    have "lprod z = e" using zr rotate_lprod[OF xsT ne ev] by simp
    moreover have "set z \<subseteq> G" using zr xsT by simp
    moreover have "length z = p" using zr len by simp
    ultimately show "z \<in> X_set p" unfolding X_set_def T_set_def by simp
  qed
  have rot_pow: "\<forall>xs\<in>X_set p. (rotate1 ^^ p) xs = xs"
  proof
    fix xs assume xsX: "xs \<in> X_set p"
    then have len: "length xs = p" unfolding X_set_def T_set_def by auto
    have "(rotate1 ^^ p) xs = rotate p xs" by (simp add: rotate_def)
    also have "\<dots> = xs" using len by simp
    finally show "(rotate1 ^^ p) xs = xs" .
  qed
  have orb0 := orbit_mod[where f = rotate1, OF pp, rule_format]
  have orb: "card (X_set p) mod p = card {xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs} mod p"
    using orb0 le_refl finX rot_sub rot_pow by blast
  have cX0: "card (X_set p) mod p = 0" using cardX by (simp add: dvd_eq_mod_eq_0)
  have rF: "replicate p e \<in> {xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs}"
  proof -
    have "set (replicate p e) \<subseteq> G" using unit_closed by (simp add: subset_iff)
    moreover have "length (replicate p e) = p" by simp
    moreover have "lprod (replicate p e) = e" by (simp add: lprod_replicate pow_e)
    ultimately show ?thesis unfolding X_set_def T_set_def by simp
  qed
  have ex: "\<exists>xs \<in> {xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs}. xs \<noteq> replicate p e"
  proof (rule ccontr)
    assume "\<not> (\<exists>xs \<in> {xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs}. xs \<noteq> replicate p e)"
    then have "{xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs} = {replicate p e}" using rF by blast
    then have "card {xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs} = 1" by simp
    then have "card {xs \<in> X_set p. rotate1 xs = xs} mod p = 1"
      using p1 by (simp add: mod_less)
    with orb cX0 show False by simp
  qed
  then obtain xs where xsF: "xs \<in> X_set p" and rxs: "rotate1 xs = xs"
    and xsr: "xs \<noteq> replicate p e" by blast
  have xsT: "set xs \<subseteq> G" and len: "length xs = p" and ev: "lprod xs = e"
    using xsF unfolding X_set_def T_set_def by auto
  have ne: "xs \<noteq> []" using len p1 by auto
  have "xs = [] \<or> card (set xs) = 1" using rotate1_fixpoint_card[OF rxs] by blast
  then have card1: "card (set xs) = 1" using ne by blast
  obtain a where sa: "set xs = {a}" using card1 by (rule card_1_singletonE)
  have all_a: "replicate (length xs) a = xs"
    by (rule replicate_length_same) (simp add: sa)
  have aG: "a \<in> G" using xsT sa by auto
  have pa: "pow a p = e"
  proof -
    have "pow a p = lprod (replicate p a)" by (simp add: lprod_replicate)
    also have "\<dots> = e" using all_a len ev by simp
    finally show ?thesis .
  qed
  have ane: "a \<noteq> e"
  proof
    assume "a = e"
    then have "xs = replicate p e" using all_a len by simp
    with xsr show False by simp
  qed
  show ?thesis
  proof (intro bexI conjI allI impI)
    show "pow a p = e" by (rule pa)
  next
    fix k
    assume k0: "0 < k" and kp: "k < p" and ek: "pow a k = e"
    have per: "(mult a ^^ p) e = e" by (simp only: pow_iter pa)
    have mm: "(mult a ^^ k) e = e" by (simp only: pow_iter ek)
    have "mult a e = e" by (rule prime_orbit_fixed[OF pp per mm k0 kp])
    then have "a \<cdot> e = e" by simp
    then have "a = e" using aG runit by metis
    with ane show False by blast
  next
    show "a \<in> G" by (rule aG)
  qed
qed

end
